subject: astronomy
title: Space Exploration: First Steps
welcome_lead: From the first satellite to people on the Moon — meet the pioneers of space.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: history of space, Sputnik, Apollo, ISS.
final_note: Every space mission stood on the shoulders of the one before.

concepts.def: Anything in orbit, natural or man-made.
A person trained to go to space.
Vehicle that pushes itself with hot gases.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957 was the first human-made satellite. It beeped from orbit and started the space age.
In 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon. Buzz Aldrin followed; Michael Collins orbited above.
The ISS has been continuously occupied since 2000. Crews from many countries do science in microgravity, orbiting Earth every 90 minutes.

mcqs.q: Where is our Solar System located in the Milky Way?
options: Right at the centre of the galaxy.
About two-thirds of the way out from the centre, in one of the spiral arms.
Where humans could survive without spacesuits.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.

mcqs.q: What is the 'habitable zone' around a star?
options: The region where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface.
Where humans could survive without spacesuits.
